source_entries.question_prompt: Q1. Which combination indicates that car K starts southeast of car L’s destination?
source_entries.independent_reasoning: In i, B%L places L’s destination at A. K&A means K turns right and reaches A, so K starts at C. C (east) is southeast of A (north).
source_entries.source_key: Compared after independent solving; no unresolved key conflict for these selected records.
source_entries.question_text:
At a square intersection, A is north, B west, C east and D south. G&H means car G starts at a fixed point, turns right and reaches H; G%H means car H starts at G, turns left and reaches a fixed point; G$H means car G starts at H, turns right and reaches a fixed point; G@H means car H starts at a fixed point, turns left and reaches G; G+H means car G starts at a fixed point and goes straight to H; G#H means car H starts at G and goes straight to a fixed point.
Q1. Which combination indicates that car K starts southeast of car L’s destination?
source_entries.explanation: In i, B%L places L’s destination at A. K&A means K turns right and reaches A, so K starts at C. C (east) is southeast of A (north).

source_entries.source: Direction and Distance 01  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 8, Q2; coded directions
source_entries.question_prompt: Q2. Which expressions indicate that car J started at C and reached A? (a) D@J + A; (b) C#J@A; (c) C%J#A.
source_entries.independent_reasoning: Applying the operator definitions in order, (a) is the only expression that establishes both endpoints C and A; (b) and (c) do not.

source_entries.question_text:
At a square intersection, A is north, B west, C east and D south. G&H means car G starts at a fixed point, turns right and reaches H; G%H means car H starts at G, turns left and reaches a fixed point; G$H means car G starts at H, turns right and reaches a fixed point; G@H means car H starts at a fixed point, turns left and reaches G; G+H means car G starts at a fixed point and goes straight to H; G#H means car H starts at G and goes straight to a fixed point.
Q2. Which expressions indicate that car J started at C and reached A? (a) D@J + A; (b) C#J@A; (c) C%J#A.
source_entries.explanation: Applying the operator definitions in order, (a) is the only expression that establishes both endpoints C and A; (b) and (c) do not.

source_entries.source: Direction and Distance 01  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 8, Q3; coded directions
source_entries.question_prompt: Q3. Given B%E + D@F, in which direction is F’s starting point from B, and in which direction is E’s destination from F’s starting point, respectively?
source_entries.independent_reasoning: B%E puts E’s destination at A (north); D@F puts F’s start at C (east). C is east of B and southeast of A, so the ordered pair is east, southeast.

original_practice_entries.question_text: Original Practice Question — A courier starts at O and walks north 5 km, then east 6 km, then south 3 km, then west 4 km. What are the endpoint coordinates relative to the starting point, taking east and north as positive?
original_practice_entries.explanation: East-west displacement is +2 km and north-south displacement is +2 km after cancelling opposite legs, so the endpoint coordinates are (+2, +2) km (east, north coordinates).
original_practice_entries.verification: Five distinct options; one correct option; answer independently derived and record read back from the intended local chapter.
